steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Prepare 12 muffin cups with paper liners.

Sift the flour, baking soda, baking powder, and salt into a bowl; set aside. In a large bowl, cream together butter and sugar until light and fluffy. Beat in the eggs one at a time, mixing well after each addition, then beat in the bananas and rum extract. Stir in the flour mixture. Fold in the shredded coconut and pineapple; mixing just enough to evenly distribute. Evenly divide the batter among the prepared muffin cups.
Bake in preheated oven until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean, 20 to 25 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Caribbean Banana Muffins
raw_recipe.description: With some of the native ingredients of the islands, you'll be hearing the steel drums in no time!

review.reviewBody: These muffins were very good! I left the rum extract out by mistake, and used 3/4 cup fresh pineapple, instead of dried. I'll use more next time! Also, the reviewer that pointed this out was right - the recipe makes 18 muffins, not 12 (we definitely didn't mind!).

I just loved these muffins, if you are making these make sure you use the rum ~ it really is what gives these the extra kick. I did tweak this recipe a little. I only had 2 bananas, so had to use just those. I used a mixture of white and brown sugar. I increased the rum extract to 1.5 tablespoons and the coconut I used 1/2 powdered coconut (from the asian store) and 1/2 shredded. I did'nt like the look of these muffins so decided to use my own coconut streutsel ( 1/4 cup all-purpose flour, 1 tablespoon white sugar, 3 tablespoons sweetened flaked coconut, 2 tablespoons butter simply mix all the ingredients together and put to one side). Once I filled the muffin papers to 3/4 full I added streutsel mixture to the top before putting in the oven, they really did give the finished muffins a m ore professional look. Like other reviews stated this recipe makes approx 18 good size muffins!

Very good! Our family really liked these muffins. The recipe made exactly 12 of our usual size; maybe we like larger muffins than some other people! I was afraid to use a tablespoon of rum extract, so only used a teaspoon. Next time I will trust the recipe and use a tablespoon. I used drained crushed pineapple instead of dried, substituted whole wheat flour for half of the flour amount, added a dash of nutmeg, only used half the amount of brown sugar, used coconut milk and canola oil to replace the butter, and put all the coconut on top instead of mixing it in. It was less than a cup, but we could really appreciate it more fully on top. My teenagers said we need to have these again - a true sign of a winner! Thanks for the recipe!

This was a great and easy recipe. Instead of muffins, I made a cake in a 13x9 pan. Silly me, I forgot the baking soda, and the cake still turned out and was delicious. Granted, it was a bit more dense than cake, more like bread or pound cake consistency, but it still received rave reviews. It was moist and flavorful. I made a crumble for the top out of butter, mixed spices, oats, shredded coconut, and brown sugar. It complimented the cake really well and added a nice, contrasting texture. I find it difficult to find good recipes with true carribean flavors, but this one is excellent.

I use this recipe often. I love the taste and texture the pineapple and coconut provides. I often used crushed pineapple instead of dried, reduce the sugar and use some random combination of butter, coconut oil and or apple sauce to sub for the butter. This makes a nice loaf and both the loaf and cupcakes freeze well.

Love this recipe! Best muffins I have ever had. I took the suggestions others made and made a couple changes. I used 1tsp of vanilla rather than the rum extract, 2 bananas, 15 1/2 oz can of crushed pineapple drained, 1cup of packed coconut and on top of the muffins put some brown sugar and coconut. Awesome! Great recipe.

These muffins were the most delicious muffin I have ever made. They were so moist, flavorful and easy! I did make a couple of changes. I used a tsp.of vanilla extract instead of rum..I did not have any rum. I also added 15oz.drained crushed pineapple rather than the dried pineapple and I added a crumb topping with 2 tbs. flour, 1/8 tsp. cinnamon, 1/3 cup brown sugar and 1tbs butter

These turned out tasting delicious.
I followed the recipe with the exception of the rum flavoring. I added some black walnut and some coconut as I didn't have the rum. Used fresh frozen pineapple. Made 12 muffins.

Family loved it. Makes a filling "pick me up" snack.
Added 1/2 c. pecans - walnuts would be great too.
These were the best muffins I've made in a very long time! I used dried unsweetened coconut, real rum and fresh pineapple. Awesome in January when we'd rather be on a Caribbean beach...thank you!

Great recipe. Alway try to adapt with the things that I have on hand. Found some dried pineapple in cupboard while cleaning so needed to use it up. Had only frozen butter so I used coconut oil and organic cane sugar and used 1 cup of pineapple. Didnt look like the picture but would be oh so good with a cream cheese frosting with some large coconut flakes in it...YES it made 18 nice sized muffins and I loved that they came out of the papers without sticking. Nice and dense, not crumbly~
These taste like the ones my grandmother makes back in Barbados!! Sooo good!!
Super yummy! Had to used crushed pineapple since that's all I had. Great way to use up those bananas in the freezer!
probably will make it again ..but don't make muffins that often.. usually cakes..
probably will make it again ..but don't make muffins that often.. usually cakes..
It was a great recipe I will definitely make it again when no one eats the bananas. I had a fun time with the kids making it. They loved it sooo much. So did their Dad.

Reduced rum extract to 1 teaspoon, and added 1 teaspoon of vanilla. Used toasted ribbon coconut which I crumbled before putting into batter, and sprinkled the tops of the muffins with coarse sugar crystals with a little cinnamon. Very tasty!

I just made these and they are great! I gave it 4/5 because I cut a pineapple up and in to small bits and used a cup of that rather than the dry. I also added chopped walnuts and cranberries. I did have a tiny bit left over, probably from the extra I added, but I just topped them all off with it to make bigger muffins. Great recipe, thank you!

These were really delicious, and perfect because I have a lot of dried pineapple chunks to use up. The coconut, banana and pineapple flavors blended perfectly. They were great breakfast muffins and they froze very well also. :) I will be making them again.

Excellent muffins! I thought they were perfectly moist... and, I am baffled by other reviewers who say the recipe as written makes too many muffins? I got 12 perfectly sized muffins out of the recipe as written. I agree with others that the coconut and pinapple flavors really aren't very strong. I will use rum extract next time- I used vanilla because it's all that I had on hand. I will definitely make again.
